title: Moving files and migrating to Azure
learningObjective: Identify AzCopy, Azure Storage Explorer and Azure File Sync for moving files, and Azure Migrate and Azure Data Box for migration.
foundation: AzCopy: a command-line tool to copy files to, from and between storage accounts. Good for scripts.
Azure Storage Explorer: a free desktop app (Windows, macOS, Linux) to browse and move files with a graphical interface.
Azure File Sync: keeps a Windows file server and an Azure file share in sync, so the server becomes a fast local cache.
Azure Migrate: one hub to discover, assess and move servers, databases, apps and data to Azure. Azure Data Box: a physical, rugged device Microsoft ships to you to move lots of data offline.
engineer: AzCopy: upload, download, copy between accounts, and sync (one-direction) blobs and files; authenticates with Microsoft Entra ID or SAS tokens; resumable; works across clouds (for example from Amazon S3).
Storage Explorer: uses AzCopy underneath; manage blobs, files, queues, tables, Data Lake Storage and managed disks; connect by Entra ID, keys or SAS.

Azure File Sync: centralise shares in Azure Files; keep the flexibility and performance of on-premises Windows Server; any protocol on the server (SMB, NFS, FTPS); as many caches as needed worldwide; cloud tiering keeps hot files local and tiers cold files to Azure; replace a failed server quickly.

Azure Migrate: integrated tools (Discovery and assessment, Server migration, Data Migration Assistant, Azure Database Migration Service, web app migration assistant, Azure Data Box) plus third-party ISV tools, with a central dashboard tracking progress.

Azure Data Box: about 80 TB usable per standard device; for one-time bulk migration, initial seeding before online sync, periodic uploads, or exporting data out of Azure (for disaster recovery or moving off). Data is encrypted (AES 256-bit) and wiped after upload following NIST 800-88.
Rule of thumb: transfer time = data size ÷ bandwidth. 80 TB over 100 Mbps takes about 74 days; ship a Data Box instead.

animation.caption: Estimate transfer times, then pick the right tool for each move.

example.title: A media company moves to Azure
body: It assesses 300 servers with Azure Migrate (sizing and cost), ships 400 TB of video archive on Data Box devices, and uses AzCopy nightly for new footage.
Regional offices keep a Windows file server each, synchronised by Azure File Sync with cloud tiering so only recent projects use local disk.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription (a free account works)
permissions: Reader to explore; Contributor to create resources
portal: Azure Migrate > Servers, databases and web apps: discover and assess.
Storage Sync Services > Create; register servers; create sync groups.
configuration.cli:
azcopy login
azcopy copy ./footage "https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net/raw" --recursive
azcopy sync ./footage "https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net/raw"

lab.objective: Estimate transfers and choose migration tools.
steps: Moving data and migrating tab: try different sizes and link speeds.
Moving files and migrating tab: answer every task.
expected: Large data on slow links → Data Box
File Sync keeps a local cache
failureScenarios: Sending hundreds of TB over a slow internet link
lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.symptom: Copy job fails after a network interruption.
troubleshooting.fix: AzCopy jobs can resume: azcopy jobs resume <id>.

troubleshooting.symptom: Local file server disk fills up.
troubleshooting.fix: Enable cloud tiering with a free-space policy.

comparisons.difference: AzCopy is scriptable command line; Storage Explorer is a GUI built on AzCopy.
Migrate is the assessment and migration hub; Data Box is one offline transfer option it includes.

misconceptions.myth: Azure File Sync replaces your file server entirely.
misconceptions.reality: It keeps the server as a cache synced with Azure Files.
It can export data from Azure too.

architectureDecisions: Assess before migrating with Azure Migrate.
Use Data Box when online transfer would take too long.
